messages:
Aisha: Quick heads up — competitor announced 'FastServe Pro' messaging this morning. We need to decide whether our upcoming launch leans into parity claims or leans hard on differentiated positioning (economics/reliability). Any immediate red flags?

Luca: I saw it. They call out '50% lower cost' in hero. we should avoid hard % claims unless we have identical benchmarks and configurations. :eyes:

Ben: agree. engineering can't commit to cost/latency claims without a reproducible benchmark matrix. p50/p95 across our standard prompts only. Also avoid saying 'drop-in compatible' unless shim exists.

Mina: CS is getting asks for exact routing parity from two pilots. they want the same tenant routing controls. If we don't offer parity, we'll need a clear migration/playbook.

Aisha: Proposal for launch guardrails (high level):
- Marketing: no direct competitor comparisons or unverified % claims. use phrasing like "cost-efficient inference" or "predictable inference economics".
- Product: two launch lanes — "Differentiated" (hosted + dedicated features we control) and "Compatibility" (opt-in shim for specific enterprise customers).
- Engineering: compatibility shim is opt-in per-tenant behind feature flag; ship only for Dedicated with documented limitations.
- Launch criteria: perf matrix (p50/p95), quality regression checks on canonical prompt set, documentation + migration guide, legal sign-off on copy.

Sam (design): For hero copy, I recommend avoiding price adjectives. Draft suggestion: "Serve LLMs with predictable latency and unit cost — across hosted, dedicated, and private". This keeps advantage and avoids direct price claims.

Luca: On the compatibility shim — quick estimate: 2 week spike to validate approach (adapter + token flow tests). long-term cost is maintenance. alternative is a guided adapter migration doc instead of runtime shim.

Ben: Implementation note: if we do runtime shim, add per-tenant guardrails and telemetry. sample flag: 
```
{
  "compat_mode": true,
  "compat_level": "routing-basic",
  "telemetry": ["latency_overrides", "fallback_counts"]
}
```
We should also have automatic rollback triggers if p95 > SLA by X ms for 5m.

Mina: Sales feedback: having a short-term "compatibility program" (controlled pilot with opt-in shim) would preserve renewals without exposing us to broad support burden. they'd pay for the pilot.

Aisha: OK action items and owners:
1) Luca — scope shim spike + risks (due 2462000030)
2) Ben — benchmark matrix and regression harness for launch prompts (due 2462000045)
3) Sam — draft hero and one-liner variations for PM/legal review (due 2462000040)
4) Mina — draft pilot offer and list potential customers (due 2462000050)

We'll recon in ~48h to lock lane choices and final launch copy. If anyone objects to the guardrails above, call it out now. :thumbsup:

Luca: noted, I'll post the spike ticket and link to the repo.

Ben: I'll start the perf runs and share raw numbers to the thread.

deploy-bot: Deployment to staging completed (build 2026.4.12-rc). Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/2871 :white_check_mark:

Mina: pinging partnerships to see if there's any channel pressure. thanks all.
